summary: Oleg Grabar specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton, later holding professorships at the University of Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard (1969–1990), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1990–1998).

Oliver Codrington worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and as Honorary Librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Ceylon and SOAS under G. P. Malalasekera, William Stede, and Betty Heimann. He became Head of Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon in 1943.

Oliver Hellwig works in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. He completed his habilitation under Harry Falk and held posts at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf and the University of Zurich (attested 2024–2025).
Oliver Petersen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang from around 1983 to 2003 and held a post at the Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (attested 2002).
Oliver Philipp Frey is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at and held a post at the University of Vienna.

Olivier Lacombe worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris, where he later taught (~1959–1970) before holding a post at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).
Olivier de Bernon specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied under Pierre L. Lamant and held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1991) and the University of California, Berkeley (~2002).

Olle Qvarnström works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Lund University, University of Washington, Harvard, and University of Copenhagen under Tord Olsson, Karl H. Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner, and held a post at Lund.
Olli Littunen works in Indology and religious studies as a PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Om Prakash studied Indology and history and archaeology at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and Bisheshwar Prasad. He taught at Delhi, served at Kirori Mal College, and was professor of economic history at Delhi School of Economics.

On Shionoya was a Sinology scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1906) and the University of Leipzig (~1906–1909). He held a post at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1920 to 1939.
Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Shenphen Nangwa.

Orna Almogi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at the University of Hamburg and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Osamu Hayashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg, holding faculty posts at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.
Osamu Izumoji specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba worked in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kansai University (~1950–1953) and held posts at Kansai University (~1958–1998), Kogakkan University (~1998–2002), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, and studied under Baiei Henmi. He served as a lecturer at Tohoku University (attested 1961) and at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (attested 1967).

Osborn Bergin was a linguist who studied at University College Cork, the School of Irish Learning, and University of Freiburg under Kuno Meyer and Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1940–1941).
